title: Author the three role definitions and the role-definition check
statement: Write `specialists/research.md`, `specialists/planning.md` and `specialists/validation.md` declaring name, description, tool allowlist, input contract, responsibilities, forbidden actions, output schema, exit criteria and escalation conditions, generating them from authored role prose merged with `lib/specialists/contract.mjs` rather than restating its write boundaries; add the role-definition check that fails a role with no declared tools, with a `--check` mode that compares generated bytes without writing and runs in every CI cell.
notes:
Scope settled 2026-09-18, before implementation.

SCOPE. This task owns the three role definitions and their static check. It does not own a specialist process. Two clauses were therefore moved out before any code: ACC-0072's "a real Pi run of each specialist reports an active tool set equal to the intersection of that role's declared allowlist and the measured host registry" now sits in ACC-0076, and ACC-0073's "a specialist run reports the same provider, model and thinking level as the orchestrator that delegated to it" is already covered there. ACC-0076 belongs to TSK-0053, which owns the delegation runtime and depends on this task.

NAMING. The check is the ROLE-DEFINITION check, never the "roster lint". Decision #18 and #143 settled that this project has no artifact roster: `task.role` is a plain string and the role set is derived by collecting values, which is why `schemas/task.schema.json` refuses a `role-assignment` type and why the scaffold writes "There is no roster to maintain". CMP-0035's "specialist roster" is an unrelated object - three child-agent role definitions - and a check named for the first meaning would read as contradicting a settled decision.

FORM. Generated Markdown with strict YAML frontmatter for machine-checked identity and tool declarations, then fixed sections for the input contract, responsibilities, forbidden actions, output schema, exit criteria and escalation conditions, so the files are directly usable as child prompts. Authored role prose is canonical data under `lib/specialists/`; `contractFor(role)` supplies tools, write boundaries, required signatures and forbidden actions. Generating rather than authoring the merged result is what makes drift structurally impossible to accept rather than a promise, the same trade `skills:check` already makes for the nine stage skills.
